name: Shaft hoisting (one hoisting day)
summary: Each day the hoist operators lift 540-600 tonnes of ore and some waste in 4-tonne skips from the loading pocket below the 460 m level to the skip dump at the 70 m level, where trucks chute-load it and haul it out the portal to the surface ore pad. A manual pocket operator loads every skip, a millwright examines the hoist and ropes daily, and the operator tests the brakes each shift and is relieved before eight hours at the controls. The hoist has spare capacity, so delays come from the pocket running empty, pocket hang-ups, power trips and the weekly shaft examination.

baseline.org_archetype: A single-mine Canadian gold producer running a 500-600 tonne-per-day underground longhole mine with ramp and shaft access, a 1,000-1,200 tonne-per-day mill and about 280 rotational site staff in northern Ontario.
baseline.notes: Site practice follows the Eagle River mine as described in its 2016 and 2022 technical reports, with Ontario Regulation 854 for the statutory checks. Crews work two 12-hour shifts a day on a 14-days-on, 14-days-off rotation.

trigger: The first hoist operator of the day takes over the hoist log and the loading pocket holds ore delivered by the trucks.
end_state: The day's ore is on the surface ore pad, the hoist log is written and the mine captain has countersigned it.

volume.seasonality: One case per calendar day; the mine runs 365 days a year. Summer storms add power trips; planned hoist and shaft shutdowns take one or two days a year.

evidence.note: Two 12-hour shifts 365 days a year (s. 16.10).

surge.cause: catch-up hoisting after a hoist outage or pocket hang-up leaves ore in temporary underground stockpiles

evidence.note: Author's estimate; hoist capacity is well above production (2022 s. 16.4), so backlogs are cleared in a day or two.

Six hoist operators in the organisation file. Reg. 854 s. 9(3) limits a worker to eight hours of hoist operation in 24, so two 12-hour shifts of hoisting need a relief operator; three operators per rotation cover the day.

The 2022 report says the loading pocket has not been automated, so a worker loads each skip by hand on the 460 mL; Reg. 854 s. 242(4) requires a designated competent person in charge of a shaft conveyance. Headcount of 4 (one per shift crew) and the cost, matched to the services worker, are the author's estimate.
Ore from the 70 mL skip dump is chute-loaded into underground trucks and hauled out the portal (2022 s. 16.4); about one driver per shift, or 2 FTE of the 24 truck operators.
Daily examination of the hoist exterior, ropes and safety catches, about 45 minutes a day, plus small repairs.
Resetting the hoist after power trips and electrical faults, a few call-outs a month.
Clearing hang-ups in the loading pocket and spill at the shaft bottom.
Countersigning the hoist log each working day and reviewing hoisted tonnes.

systems.name: Statutory hoist log books (Hoist Operator's Log Book, Shaft Inspection Record, Rope Record Book; paper)
Shift reports, line-up boards and production tallies (paper and spreadsheets)
Leaky feeder radio and surface radio network
Maintenance management system (ERP maintenance module or standalone)

resources.name: Production shaft hoist, skip and cage (loading pocket below 460 m level to dump at 70 m level)

steps.name: Take over the hoist and read the log book
steps.description: The incoming hoist operator reads the Hoist Operator's Log Book entries from the previous shifts, notes any defects, brake or clutch problems and restrictions, and countersigns the previous operator's entries before taking the controls.

error.defect_description: A restriction written by the previous operator is missed.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 239(1) and (2)(a): hoist operator records each shift in the Hoist Operator's Log Book and countersigns the previous entries

steps.name: Test the brakes and the overwind and underwind devices
steps.description: Before moving people or ore, the operator runs the brake tests on each drum and trips the overwind and underwind limits to confirm they stop the conveyance, and writes the results in the log book.

error.defect_description: A weak brake passes a rushed test.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 240(1)(a), (b) and (2): brakes tested at least once each shift and immediately before moving persons; overwind and underwind devices tested at least once in 24 hours of use

steps.name: Examine the hoist, ropes and conveyance safety catches
steps.description: A millwright designated as competent examines the outside of the hoist, the drums and clutches, the ropes over their visible length and the cage and skip safety catches and attachments, and signs the record book.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 248(2)(a): hoist exterior, ropes and conveyance safety catches examined each day the hoist is in use

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 248(2)(a). Assigning the daily examination to a millwright is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Run the cage for the weekly shaft and sheave examination
steps.description: Once a week the operator runs the cage slowly from the collar to the shaft bottom while the shaft crew examines the shaft, guides and sheaves and records findings in the Shaft Inspection Record. No ore is hoisted during the examination.

error.defect_description: A loose guide or damaged set noted but not reported to maintenance.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 249(1)(a) and (2) (shaft examined at least once a week and recorded) and s. 248(2.1) (sheaves and conveyance attachments examined weekly)

evidence.note: Reg. 854 ss. 248(2.1), 249. Duration is the author's estimate for a 580 m shaft.

steps.name: Repair a defect before hoisting
steps.description: The millwright or electrician repairs the defect found in the tests or examination, writes it up in the maintenance system and the log, and the hoist operator re-runs the brake and limit tests before releasing the hoist.

error.defect_description: Repair needs parts and holds for a second shift.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; hoist defects found at the start of the day are uncommon but stop all ore movement.

steps.name: Ride the shaft crew and materials on the cage
steps.description: The operator moves the loading pocket crew, shaft maintenance workers and any long or heavy materials on the six-person cage at the start of the shift, using the standard bell signals. No ore is hoisted while people ride.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 244(1) (no person transported while ore or waste is hoisted, cage doors closed), s. 236 (signal code) and s. 133(2) (explosives in a conveyance handled under immediate supervision)

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.4: one compartment has a skip over cage limited to 6 persons; most people use the ramps. Reg. 854 ss. 133(2), 236, 244.

steps.name: Signal and tend the cage at the stations
steps.description: The cagetender closes the gates, gives the cautionary, destination and executive signals to the hoist room and stays in charge of the cage while people and materials load and unload at the 70 mL station and the 460 mL pocket level.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 242(4) (designated competent person in charge of a shaft conveyance) and s. 236(3)-(4) (signal sequence and code)

steps.name: Check the loading pocket and chute gates
steps.description: At the 460 mL the pocket operator checks how full the pocket is, tests the chute gate and measuring controls, looks for oversize on the grizzly and radios the hoist room that skipping can start.

error.defect_description: Oversize left on the grizzly later hangs up the pocket.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 210(6): equipment that discharges into a skip needs actuating power before any gate opens

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.4: ore is hoisted from the loading pocket below the 460 mL, which has not been automated. Reg. 854 s. 210(6).

steps.name: Load skips at the pocket through the day shift
steps.description: For each trip the pocket operator opens the chute into the measuring flask, fills it to the 4-tonne skip load, dumps it into the waiting skip and signals the hoist room. Waste is loaded in separate runs when it is called for.

error.defect_description: Skip overloaded or ore and waste mixed in a run.

evidence.note: Certified skip payload of 4 tonnes; manual loading pocket (s. 16.4). About 70 trips a shift for 270 t; attended time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Hoist ore and waste skips to the 70 mL dump (day shift)
steps.description: The hoist operator runs the double-drum hoist in balance, one skip up while the other comes down, from the 460 mL pocket to the skip dump above the 70 mL station. He watches the depth indicators and speed and counts the trips.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 240(1)(d): operator remains at the controls while the hoist is in motion under manual control

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.4: double-drum hoist, 6 m/s, 4 t skips, realistic maximum of 16 operating hours a day, capacity well above production. Reg. 854 s. 240(1)(d).

steps.name: Wait for trucks to refill the pocket
steps.description: When the pocket runs down the hoist stops and the pocket operator radios the shift supervisor for trucks. The long ramp haul means the pocket is often empty for part of the shift.

evidence.note: Average one-way ramp haul of 6.9 km to the truck dump feeding the pocket (s. 1). Waiting time is the author's estimate.

steps.name: Clear a hang-up in the pocket or spill at the shaft bottom
steps.description: Services workers lock out the chute, bar down or water-blast bridged ore in the pocket following the written procedure, or muck out spill below the loading pocket so the skips can run. Hoisting stops until it is clear.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 84(1), (3) and (4): written procedures for removing material from passes and chutes, worker positioning and lockable chute gates

evidence.note: Reg. 854 s. 84. Frequency and duration are the author's estimate.

steps.name: Reset the hoist after a power trip
steps.description: Summer lightning and storms on the long transmission line cause power dips that trip the hoist. An electrician checks the drive and protection relays and resets them, and the operator re-tests the brakes before moving people.

error.defect_description: Underlying drive fault mistaken for a power dip.

evidence.note: Author's estimate; remote northern Ontario mines on single transmission lines lose power several times a year, mostly in summer storms. The 2022 report notes the hoist drive and controls were upgraded in 2020.

steps.name: Hand the hoist to the relief operator
steps.description: Before reaching eight hours at the controls, the operator writes his shift entries, briefs the relieving operator on trips, faults and the pocket level, and the relief operator countersigns and takes over.

error.defect_description: A fault mentioned verbally is not written down.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 9(3) (no more than eight hours of hoist operation in any 24) and s. 239(2)(a) (countersigning previous entries)

steps.name: Load skips at the pocket through the night shift
steps.description: The night-shift pocket operator loads skips from the pocket as trucks deliver, keeping ore and waste runs separate and noting the number of skips of each.

error.defect_description: Skip overloaded or ore and waste mixed.

evidence.note: Manual loading pocket (s. 16.4). Night shift hoists a little less because development waste is trucked to stopes on days.

steps.name: Hoist ore and waste skips to the 70 mL dump (night shift)
steps.description: The relief hoist operator continues skipping through the night shift as the pocket fills, stopping for the end-of-shift blast and for any shaft work, and counts the trips by type.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 240(1)(d): operator remains at the controls while the hoist is in motion under manual control

evidence.note: Section 16.4.

steps.name: Chute-load trucks at the 70 mL and haul out the portal
steps.description: Truck drivers load from the chute under the 70 mL skip dump and haul the ore out the portal to the surface ore pad, where it is later reloaded into surface trucks for the 16.6 km haul to the mill. Touch time is the elapsed truck time over the day.

error.defect_description: Loads counted against the wrong day or pad.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 105.1 and s. 106: traffic management program and ramp traffic control

evidence.note: 2022 s. 16.4: trucks load at a truck chute and haul ore out the portal to a surface pad, then surface trucks haul 16.6 km to the mill. Truck time is the author's estimate for about 18-20 loads a day.

steps.name: Write the shift entries in the hoist log
steps.description: Each operator records hours run, trips, delays, faults, brake and clutch condition and any rope or shaft observations in the Hoist Operator's Log Book before leaving the hoist room.

error.defect_description: Delay causes left out, so hoist availability is overstated.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 239(1): report of each shift in the Hoist Operator's Log Book

steps.name: Compile hoisted tonnes for the day
steps.description: The day-shift hoist operator adds up skips of ore and waste from both shifts, multiplies by the skip factor and types the totals into the daily production spreadsheet for the mine captain.

error.defect_description: Skip factor or skip count wrong, so hoisted tonnes differ from trucked and milled tonnes.

evidence.note: 4 t certified skip payload (s. 16.4). Skip-count tonnage is common practice (author's estimate).

steps.name: Countersign the log and review hoisted tonnes
steps.description: The mine captain reads and countersigns the hoist log, compares hoisted tonnes with the truck tallies and the plan at the morning meeting, and asks about delays.

control.basis: Ontario Regulation 854 s. 239(4): supervisor countersigns the Hoist Operator's Log Book each working day

steps.name: Investigate a hoisting shortfall
steps.description: The mine captain finds why tonnes were short or did not match (pocket hang-up, trucks short, hoist down, counting error), arranges a fix such as an extra truck or a pocket clean-out, and notes it for the reconciliation.

evidence.note: Author's estimate.

exceptions.name: Weekly shaft examination
exceptions.description: The hoist runs the cage slowly for the weekly shaft and sheave examination and does not hoist ore for several hours.

exceptions.name: Defect at start of day
exceptions.description: A failed brake or limit test or a defect found in the daily examination stops hoisting until repaired and re-tested.

exceptions.name: Pocket runs empty
exceptions.description: Trucks cannot keep up with the hoist and the pocket runs down.

exceptions.name: Pocket hang-up or shaft spill
exceptions.description: Bridged ore or spill below the pocket stops skipping until services workers clear it.

exceptions.name: Power trip
exceptions.description: A storm-related power dip trips the hoist and an electrician resets it.

benchmarks.unit: calendar days from the first operator's log take-over to the captain countersigning the log

evidence.note: A hoisting day runs over 24 hours and the log is countersigned at the next morning meeting.

benchmarks.population: Eagle River hoist at 540-600 t a day

evidence.note: Calculated by the author: 4 t skips, 6 m/s, about 390 m from the 460 mL pocket to the 70 mL dump gives roughly a 2.5-minute trip, so 140-150 trips a day take 6-7 hours, against a realistic maximum of 16 operating hours (s. 16.4).

benchmarks.unit: tonnes per day on 20 operating hours from a 420 m hoisting depth

evidence.note: Underground mining fleet and hoist section.

pain_points.description: The hoist has far more capacity than the trucks can feed it, so it often waits for ore while the operator and pocket operator must stay on station.

evidence.note: Capacity greatly exceeds planned production (s. 16.4); long ramp haul to the pocket (s. 1).

pain_points.description: The manual loading pocket needs an operator for every skip and is the usual place for hang-ups; the technical report recommends automating any new pocket.

evidence.note: Sections 1 and 16.4: the loading pocket has not been automated; any new loading pocket should be automated.

pain_points.description: Hoisted ore is rehandled twice more before the mill: chute-loaded into underground trucks at the 70 mL, then reloaded on the surface pad for a 16.6 km road haul.

evidence.note: Section 16.4.

pain_points.description: The eight-hour limit on hoist operation means each 12-hour shift needs a relief operator, so hoisting is staffed with three operators per rotation for a hoist that runs six to eight hours a day.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Gold Mining Complex, Ontario, Canada (SRK project CAPR001445, effective 31 December 2021)
sources.publisher: SRK Consulting (Canada) Inc. for Wesdome Gold Mines Ltd.
sources.supports: Three-compartment shaft with a skip-over-cage limited to 6 persons, main station at 70 mL with the skip dump above it, loading pocket below the 460 mL, shaft bottom at 580 mL; CIR double-drum hoist, 6 m/s, 4 t certified skip payload, controls upgraded in 2020, loading pocket not automated, 16 realistic operating hours a day with capacity well above production; ore chute-loaded into underground trucks at the 70 mL and hauled out the portal, then 16.6 km by surface truck to the mill; most personnel use the ramps; two 12-hour shifts 365 days a year; 6.9 km ramp haul to the pocket.

sources.title: Technical Report for the Eagle River Mining Complex including the Eagle River Gold Mine, the Mishi Gold Mine and related infrastructure (Mannard and Ng)
sources.supports: Hoist rated at about 3,100 t a day on 20 operating hours from a 420 m hoisting depth, 8,800 lb payload.

sources.title: R.R.O. 1990, Reg. 854: Mines and Mining Plants, Occupational Health and Safety Act (e-Laws consolidation in force 1 July 2021, archived copy captured 17 January 2022)
sources.publisher: Government of Ontario (archived by the Library and Archives Canada web archive)
sources.supports: Eight-hour limit on hoist operation (s. 9(3)), log books (ss. 207, 239), brake and overwind tests (s. 240), operator at the controls (s. 240(1)(d)), daily and weekly hoist and conveyance examinations (s. 248), weekly shaft examination and Shaft Inspection Record (s. 249), signals (s. 236), conveyance attendant (s. 242(4)), no persons with ore (s. 244), explosives in conveyances (s. 133(2)), skip loading controls (s. 210(6)), chute and pass procedures (s. 84), traffic management (ss. 105.1, 106).

assumptions: At this mine the shaft hoists ore from the 460 mL loading pocket to a skip dump above the 70 mL station, not to a surface headframe bin; trucks then carry the ore out the portal. The organisation file's description (skipping to surface bins) is corrected here, and the portal haul from the 70 mL is included because it is what delivers hoisted ore to the surface stockpile.

The organisation file has no loading pocket operator or cagetender; the role is added with not_in_org_file because the pocket is manual and Reg. 854 requires a competent person in charge of the conveyance.
Personnel mostly travel by ramp, so man-hoisting at shift change is small; this differs from the organisation file's description of moving people at shift change.

Pocket loading and skipping (s09 with s10, s15 with s16) and the portal truck haul (s17) run at the same time and are linked with concurrent_with, so the simulated day (median about 1.1 days including the wait for the captain's countersignature) stays close to the 1.0-day benchmark.
Hoist operator touch time is time attending the controls while skipping, which includes waiting for skips to be loaded; actual skipping is about 6.5 hours a day.

Stated FTE (about 12) is above the hands-on estimate (about 7) because the hoist and the manual pocket must be staffed through both shifts whenever ore may arrive, and Reg. 854 s. 9(3) forces a relief operator each 12-hour shift; idle attended time between truck arrivals is not all counted as touch time.

Daily examination by a millwright, frequencies of pocket hang-ups, power trips and the weekly examination duration are the author's estimates; the weekly shaft examination itself belongs to mnt-hoist-inspection and appears here only as hoist time lost to production.

Notes above that describe a mismatch refer to the file before the correction.
